svg.title: The ORM scale wall: an object-relational mapper wins in the startup phase and hits a wall at scale
svg.desc: Two panels showing the same tool at two stages. Left, the startup phase (cyan): an ORM like SQLAlchemy turns Python objects into database rows with no SQL, so you ship features in minutes, and it hides the details. Right, the scale phase (amber, a caution): across many users and distributed machines those same hidden details cause silent failures that can corrupt data, so you need the control of raw SQL. The lesson is that the ORM trades control for speed, which is a good deal early and a liability at scale. Color key: cyan is the startup win where the ORM saves time, amber is the caution at scale where its hidden details become dangerous.
svg.text: The same hidden details that save time early corrupt data at scale

g.text: Ship features in minutes, no SQL to write
The ORM writes the queries for you
It hides a lot of details
the hidden details stay out of your way
the hidden details now run across nodes
Hidden queries fire N+1 times, silently
You need raw-SQL control to fix it
know the SQL, then choose ORM vs raw

svg.text: Cyan: startup win, the ORM saves time. Amber: caution at scale, its hidden details become dangerous.
